objective: Using ticket B's outcome, prove that counting maps to the four-way group with bounded first homology is #P-hard (a gadget for the Massey four-form, a partition-function reduction and anchor isolation), or prove a polynomial algorithm, or record a substantive obstruction; state the resulting class-3 criterion (graded hard pairs versus irreducible interactions of three or more) with its precise gaps.
status: Proved by BEYOND-CLASS2-20261027-001C-P001: for p >= 5, counting maps from pi1 of 2-surgeries on knots (H1 = Z/2) into G_p = U4(F_p) x| <diag(1,-1,1,-1)> is #P-hard, although at r = 2 no group has a hard pair and every coprime class-2 group is polynomial. The count is 1 + p^(N+4) times the number of class triples with vanishing four-way (triple Massey) form, read through the J-duality of Burau at -1. Cabled pure braids with conjugators in the third term steer it exactly by their degree-3 Magnus tensor, and dihedral symmetric powers make the base vanish. The gadget gives |Hom| = 1 + p^(12m+4) Z_f with f(0) = p^12 and f(0,0,0,1) = p^6(2p^4 - p^2), and Bulatov-Grohe applies to f^2. Checks over Z and at four primes pass; realization supported by BEYOND-CLASS2-20261027-001B-E001.
title: Decide the four-way case: hardness or tractability of triple-Massey counting
